ANDROID MAINTENANCE / READ-ONLY CHECKS

Check Android update safety

For people who maintain approved sideloaded apps when device rules or recovery paths change.

Try it with sample data

See a redacted report and the next safe step.

Read-only adb checks
Device IDs are redacted
Free for one device
Sample readiness report
READINESS REPORT / SAMPLE
device-6f31a0b2 · Android 15 (sample)
83% · Fix one item before recovery
Authorized USB debugging
READY

One authorized sample device is visible to adb.
Next: Keep the authorization prompt accepted while checking.

Developer options
READY

Developer options are enabled.
Next: Leave this unchanged for approved maintenance.

USB data mode
READY

The sample device exposes adb over USB.
Next: Use a data-capable cable if this changes.

Free data storage
READY

2.8 GiB free on /data. The 1 GiB safety floor is met.
Next: Keep the floor before copying an update.

Package signer match
READY

The installed sample signer SHA-256 matches the expected approved signer.
Next: Keep the approved APK and signer digest with this report.

Recovery update visibility
NEEDS REVIEW

A/B update support is visible, but Android cannot safely prove recovery sideload status while running.
Next: Read your device’s approved recovery instructions before using recovery.

Recovery checklist
Keep the approved APK and its known-good version.
Record the app package and signer before an update.
Stop after an error and save the report before retrying.
Install the command-line tool
$ sideload-readiness demo --output readiness.md
Wrote readiness.md

$ sideload-readiness check --package com.example.approved
  --expected-signer 9A:25:70:…
83% — Signer matched. Review recovery before updating.

The command asks adb for status. It does not install apps, unlock devices, or change Android settings.

The macOS package and Windows app are unsigned. Verify the matching Sigstore bundle before installation.

Open release downloads
Linux and macOS installer
PowerShell installer

Checking published downloads.

How the readiness check works
01
Connect one Android device

Accept Android’s USB debugging prompt. Choose a device when adb lists more than one.

02
Check device and app readiness

Compare the installed signer SHA-256 with the approved APK. Read storage, USB state, and recovery clues.

03
Follow the report’s next step

Save a redacted report. Follow its next step or stop before an update.

What this tool does and does not do
What the CLI checks

Make a device-specific report from read-only adb queries. It explains what to check next.

What the CLI never does

It never bypasses Android controls, unlocks bootloaders, or distributes APKs.
